key_impacts: 3,520 houses washed away and 1,800 houses partially damaged in Dakshin Bedkashi
Coastal embankment overtopped and breached in six places
20.55 km of embankment damaged (of 27.37 km) causing widespread inundation
evidence_snippets: Cyclone Aila hit the Bangladesh coast on 25 May 2009 with a 2–6 m storm surge.
Koyra upazila was one of the worst affected areas by cyclone Aila.
In Dakshin Bedkashi, Aila killed 33 people and washed away 3,520 houses; 1,800 were partially damaged.

key_impacts: Villages inundated twice daily by tidal water until 2013
Prolonged inundation across almost the entire union
Recovery of housing and other sectors delayed
evidence_snippets: Dakshin Bedkashi suffered prolonged inundation due to breaching of polders by the storm surge.
Villages were inundated twice a day by tidal water until rehabilitation of coastal polders in 2013.
As a result, housing recovery and other sector recovery was delayed.
